speaker: Michael R. Williams
text: West Virginia, as you know, I think --

case_name: West Virginia, Et Al., Petitioners, V. B.p.j., By Her Next Friend And Mother, Heather Jackson, Respondent
speaker: GORSUCH
text: So why -- why isn't it in your brief?

case_name: West Virginia, Et Al., Petitioners, V. B.p.j., By Her Next Friend And Mother, Heather Jackson, Respondent
speaker: Michael R. Williams
text: West Virginia is maybe uniquely a fan of clear statement rules, as Your Honor might know from past cases, but in the Spending Clause context, I think it is, in fact, the case that your Court has repeatedly stressed that Congress has to speak without exception --

case_name: West Virginia, Et Al., Petitioners, V. B.p.j., By Her Next Friend And Mother, Heather Jackson, Respondent
speaker: GORSUCH
text: I know what we've said. I'm wondering about what you didn't say.

case_name: West Virginia, Et Al., Petitioners, V. B.p.j., By Her Next Friend And Mother, Heather Jackson, Respondent
speaker: Michael R. Williams
text: So I think, if you're looking at the way that West Virginia has characterized it, certainly, we have made that argument and presented that argument to this Court. I'd refer you to the topside brief. It's clear and centered under a clear heading. As  -- I think what their suggestion is from the other side is that we didn't clearly enough  raise that argument below. We would take issue with that characterization. There was obviously binding contrary authority in the Fourth Circuit. And so I think, strategically, we decided not to make that the front-and-center argument because we understood that was dead on arrival in  that particular court. But that's not to say that we waived the issue by any means. It's a canon of construction that continues to assist this Court in its application of the text of the statute.

case_name: West Virginia, Et Al., Petitioners, V. B.p.j., By Her Next Friend And Mother, Heather Jackson, Respondent
speaker: JACKSON
text: But, counsel, can I just ask you about this, though?  Have we ever applied the Spending Clause's notice requirement  outside of the damages context? Because, here, we're not talking about a situation in which B.P.G. is seeking damages,  and I thought that was sort of a crux of the Spending Clause analysis.

case_name: West Virginia, Et Al., Petitioners, V. B.p.j., By Her Next Friend And Mother, Heather Jackson, Respondent
speaker: Michael R. Williams
text: I will concede, Your Honor, that many of the cases that talk about this arise in the context of -- or maybe even all of --

case_name: West Virginia, Et Al., Petitioners, V. B.p.j., By Her Next Friend And Mother, Heather Jackson, Respondent
speaker: JACKSON
text: All of them.

case_name: West Virginia, Et Al., Petitioners, V. B.p.j., By Her Next Friend And Mother, Heather Jackson, Respondent
speaker: Michael R. Williams
text: All of the cases arise in the context --

case_name: West Virginia, Et Al., Petitioners, V. B.p.j., By Her Next Friend And Mother, Heather Jackson, Respondent
speaker: JACKSON
text: Yes. Thank you.

case_name: West Virginia, Et Al., Petitioners, V. B.p.j., By Her Next Friend And Mother, Heather Jackson, Respondent
speaker: Michael R. Williams
text: I'll concede as much, yes, Your Honor. But I don't think the Court has ever suggested that the specific request for damages is the reason for its analysis. And I think that actually would be inconsistent  --

case_name: West Virginia, Et Al., Petitioners, V. B.p.j., By Her Next Friend And Mother, Heather Jackson, Respondent
speaker: JACKSON
text: But we would be having to address that, I guess, and extend it in the -- in this context if we were to take a Spending Clause tack.

case_name: West Virginia, Et Al., Petitioners, V. B.p.j., By Her Next Friend And Mother, Heather Jackson, Respondent
speaker: Michael R. Williams
text: I would respectfully disagree, Your Honor. I would say that jus t because the Court hasn't done so before doesn't mean it's an extension per se. I think that what the Court has said is that you view the language of these statutes as effectively contractual agreements. And I think that that same sort of contractual logic applies whether  you're asking the state to pay out damages or whether you're asking it to take specific  action under compulsion of action.

case_name: West Virginia, Et Al., Petitioners, V. B.p.j., By Her Next Friend And Mother, Heather Jackson, Respondent
speaker: JACKSON
text: So -- so who's the -- who -- who -- who is the contract between here?  And  -- and I thought the regulated party needs to know what it's agreeing to so it can consent, but, here, the regulated party is the schools and it's the state that's coming in. So I'm just trying to understand how the Spending Clause analysis works in this context.

case_name: West Virginia, Et Al., Petitioners, V. B.p.j., By Her Next Friend And Mother, Heather Jackson, Respondent
speaker: Michael R. Williams
text: So I think the state is certainly one party that does receive federal educational funds, but it's also the many other Petitioners that stand before you, incl uding the county school board and the state school board, are also Petitioners in this case. I think there would certainly be  --if anybody were clearly bound by the condi tions of Title IX, it would be --

case_name: West Virginia, Et Al., Petitioners, V. B.p.j., By Her Next Friend And Mother, Heather Jackson, Respondent
speaker: JACKSON
text: So it would map on. I mean, I guess I'm  -- I'm worried that --

case_name: West Virginia, Et Al., Petitioners, V. B.p.j., By Her Next Friend And Mother, Heather Jackson, Respondent
speaker: Michael R. Williams
text: Right.

case_name: West Virginia, Et Al., Petitioners, V. B.p.j., By Her Next Friend And Mother, Heather Jackson, Respondent
speaker: JACKSON
text: -- this might actually implicate the question that we didn't resolve in Moyle, and so we'd have to kind of figure that out because it seems like it's a different set of facts than the typical  Spending Clause application.

case_name: West Virginia, Et Al., Petitioners, V. B.p.j., By Her Next Friend And Mother, Heather Jackson, Respondent
speaker: Michael R. Williams
text: I think, if anything, Your Honor, this is maybe easier than your typical Spending Clause analysis because you've got everybody from the state all the way down to the local county school board, anybody and everybody who's involved in this case is a party to this action. In fact, you resolved a petition for cert from the Athletics Commission saying we're not actually a state actor, and the Fourth Circuit saw things quite differently. So I think there's really no concern in this case that you have an absent actor problem when it comes to  the Spending Clause analysis. And, ultimately, of course, if it's just a canon of construction, if you're looking for a clear  statement, then I think it would apply regardless of the particular party who might be in front of you because the statute applies across the board. You know, the regulated party is going to be affected  regardless of whether they happen to be in front of you in the given case.

case_name: West Virginia, Et Al., Petitioners, V. B.p.j., By Her Next Friend And Mother, Heather Jackson, Respondent
speaker: BARRETT
text: Counsel, can I ask you a --

case_name: West Virginia, Et Al., Petitioners, V. B.p.j., By Her Next Friend And Mother, Heather Jackson, Respondent
speaker: SOTOMAYOR
text: I presume --

case_name: West Virginia, Et Al., Petitioners, V. B.p.j., By Her Next Friend And Mother, Heather Jackson, Respondent
speaker: BARRETT
text: Go ahead.

case_name: West Virginia, Et Al., Petitioners, V. B.p.j., By Her Next Friend And Mother, Heather Jackson, Respondent
speaker: SOTOMAYOR
text: I'm sorry. I presume that if it's statutory construction, a canon of statutory construction, it's hard to say you can waive that.

case_name: West Virginia, Et Al., Petitioners, V. B.p.j., By Her Next Friend And Mother, Heather Jackson, Respondent
speaker: Michael R. Williams
text: It  -- it's very hard to say you can waive that, Your Honor, yes.

case_name: West Virginia, Et Al., Petitioners, V. B.p.j., By Her Next Friend And Mother, Heather Jackson, Respondent
speaker: BARRETT
text: I just wanted to ask if, on your understanding of Title IX, you could have separated by sex classrooms in biology or in math based on some evidence that you have that say men are better at math and science. What are the -- what are the the limits to your Title IX theory?

case_name: West Virginia, Et Al., Petitioners, V. B.p.j., By Her Next Friend And Mother, Heather Jackson, Respondent
speaker: Michael R. Williams
text: So I -- I think your instinct there in part arises from the fact that we're skeptical of any notion that there are inherent differences. So I want to kind of acknowledge the -- the real reality of the situation.

case_name: West Virginia, Et Al., Petitioners, V. B.p.j., By Her Next Friend And Mother, Heather Jackson, Respondent
speaker: BARRETT
text: Well, your whole position in this case depends on there being  inherent differences, right?

case_name: West Virginia, Et Al., Petitioners, V. B.p.j., By Her Next Friend And Mother, Heather Jackson, Respondent
speaker: Michael R. Williams
text: It does. And I think that that's exactly why discrimination in the Title IX context, where it acknowledges merely inherent biological differences, that that's not discrimination. That's a distinction. And I think that's consistent with this Court's longstanding understanding of what discrimination means. It looks to differential treatment of similarly situated individuals. So even in a case like North Haven, you're talking about differential treatment of similarly situated individuals. So, if we're talking about in an athletic context, you're not addressing similarly situated individuals. And I think, again, the Javits Amendment and the regulations that flowed from the Javits Amendment are a realistic reflection of those --

case_name: West Virginia, Et Al., Petitioners, V. B.p.j., By Her Next Friend And Mother, Heather Jackson, Respondent
speaker: SOTOMAYOR
text: Could you go  --

case_name: West Virginia, Et Al., Petitioners, V. B.p.j., By Her Next Friend And Mother, Heather Jackson, Respondent
speaker: Michael R. Williams
text: --meaningful biological differences.

case_name: West Virginia, Et Al., Petitioners, V. B.p.j., By Her Next Friend And Mother, Heather Jackson, Respondent
speaker: SOTOMAYOR
text: What's your answer --

case_name: West Virginia, Et Al., Petitioners, V. B.p.j., By Her Next Friend And Mother, Heather Jackson, Respondent
speaker: BARRETT
text: But the Javits Amendment gives you a reason in the sports context you need to do it.

case_name: West Virginia, Et Al., Petitioners, V. B.p.j., By Her Next Friend And Mother, Heather Jackson, Respondent
speaker: Michael R. Williams
text: Right.

case_name: West Virginia, Et Al., Petitioners, V. B.p.j., By Her Next Friend And Mother, Heather Jackson, Respondent
speaker: BARRETT
text: I'm just wondering whether, you know, your friends on the other side have basically conceded that Title IX allows sex -separated sports teams, so I don't know that we need to really get into that. I'd be a little bit concerned about what the ramifications of that might be. And the Javits Amendment in the context of sports makes a difference anyway, but more broadly, I mean, if  -- if --if some  --if a state produced some studies saying, listen, you know, women's presence in, you know, calculus is holding men back because they're so much more capable and they can just move so much more quickly, seems to me like there would be some risk on your understanding that that would be okay.

case_name: West Virginia, Et Al., Petitioners, V. B.p.j., By Her Next Friend And Mother, Heather Jackson, Respondent
speaker: Michael R. Williams
text: I think, again, realistically, Your Honor, that would almost certainly fail on the lack of --

case_name: West Virginia, Et Al., Petitioners, V. B.p.j., By Her Next Friend And Mother, Heather Jackson, Respondent
speaker: KAGAN
text: Well, how about chess club?

case_name: West Virginia, Et Al., Petitioners, V. B.p.j., By Her Next Friend And Mother, Heather Jackson, Respondent
speaker: Michael R. Williams
text: A chess distinction, I think, again, might fail because there's an actual lack of evidence of meaningful physiological differences that are reflected in the existence of the express regulations in the athletics context.

case_name: West Virginia, Et Al., Petitioners, V. B.p.j., By Her Next Friend And Mother, Heather Jackson, Respondent
speaker: KAGAN
text: I mean, I think a lot of people would say, you know, if you look at the ranks of chess Grand Masters, there are not a whole lot of women there, and, you know, what does that mean?  Well  --

case_name: West Virginia, Et Al., Petitioners, V. B.p.j., By Her Next Friend And Mother, Heather Jackson, Respondent
speaker: Michael R. Williams
text: Well, I  --I think --

case_name: West Virginia, Et Al., Petitioners, V. B.p.j., By Her Next Friend And Mother, Heather Jackson, Respondent
speaker: KAGAN

case_name: West Virginia, Et Al., Petitioners, V. B.p.j., By Her Next Friend And Mother, Heather Jackson, Respondent
speaker: Michael R. Williams
text: Right.

case_name: West Virginia, Et Al., Petitioners, V. B.p.j., By Her Next Friend And Mother, Heather Jackson, Respondent
speaker: KAGAN
text: You know, I  -- I think that there's a sort of intuitive -- I think there are a lot of chess Grand Masters who would tell you that women just like for whatever reason, they're  --you know, they don't -- they're not very -- they're not as good as this.

case_name: West Virginia, Et Al., Petitioners, V. B.p.j., By Her Next Friend And Mother, Heather Jackson, Respondent
speaker: Michael R. Williams
text: I -- I think chess is an interestingly closer question. I've come to understand just recently, in fact, that there  are sex distinctions in the elite --

case_name: West Virginia, Et Al., Petitioners, V. B.p.j., By Her Next Friend And Mother, Heather Jackson, Respondent
speaker: GORSUCH
text: Well, let's -- let's -- you're fighting that hypothetical. And I -- I guess the question really is, okay, Title IX says you can't discriminate on the basis of sex.

case_name: West Virginia, Et Al., Petitioners, V. B.p.j., By Her Next Friend And Mother, Heather Jackson, Respondent
speaker: Michael R. Williams
text: Yes, Your Honor.

case_name: West Virginia, Et Al., Petitioners, V. B.p.j., By Her Next Friend And Mother, Heather Jackson, Respondent
speaker: GORSUCH
text: I understand what that means. I think I do, right?  Can't treat men and women differently. Okay, all right, fine. You're saying, ah, but it matters whether they're similarly situated. And your friends in the government like that line too. Well, there's -- you know, I've got a lot of evidence that  --that girls perform a lot better in high school than boys, okay? There's a lot of scientific evidence, whatever, all right?  Let's just posit that, all right?  Well, so I'm going to have a special remedial program for boys and the women can't come and  -- because they're not similarly situated. Why on earth would Title IX care about that?  It says you can't discriminate on the basis of sex in a program or activity of  your educational institution.

case_name: West Virginia, Et Al., Petitioners, V. B.p.j., By Her Next Friend And Mother, Heather Jackson, Respondent
speaker: Michael R. Williams
text: So I think that --

case_name: West Virginia, Et Al., Petitioners, V. B.p.j., By Her Next Friend And Mother, Heather Jackson, Respondent
speaker: GORSUCH
text: Why  -- why put that gloss on it?

case_name: West Virginia, Et Al., Petitioners, V. B.p.j., By Her Next Friend And Mother, Heather Jackson, Respondent
speaker: Michael R. Williams
text: And  --and, Your Honor, I want to be clear. I think the task for the Court today is somewhat easier in part because of the express regulations that they have actually not challenged and that do expressly contemplate exactly what West Virginia has done. So I think your  --your hypothetical, yes, of course, is there, but I think the reality is that Congress and the agency have together kind of addressed this specific question in a way that makes this Court's task much easier. But I think the  --the problem may be with your --

case_name: West Virginia, Et Al., Petitioners, V. B.p.j., By Her Next Friend And Mother, Heather Jackson, Respondent
speaker: GORSUCH
text: There may be another answer. We don't need to rely on this similarly situated argument?  Is that what you're trying to tell me, counsel?

case_name: West Virginia, Et Al., Petitioners, V. B.p.j., By Her Next Friend And Mother, Heather Jackson, Respondent
speaker: Michael R. Williams
text: I think you could also take that approach, yes, Your Honor. And I think the reality is that that hypothetical  addresses a situation that's much closer to the sort of exclusion and the specific context that gave rise to Title IX in the first place. And so I think that the Court would be much more legitimately concerned that that would detect the very problem that Congress trying to head off in passing Title IX in the first place. But I think that really kind of puts the lie to the -- the position that -- that West Virginia is somehow discriminating because it's advancing the very same purpose that Congress itself was trying to advance in enacting Title IX in the first place. I mean, that's why West Virginia somewhat deliberately made its  --its -- its law mirror the exact same language from the express regulations themselves.

case_name: West Virginia, Et Al., Petitioners, V. B.p.j., By Her Next Friend And Mother, Heather Jackson, Respondent
speaker: GORSUCH
text: I'm afraid I've got  --

case_name: West Virginia, Et Al., Petitioners, V. B.p.j., By Her Next Friend And Mother, Heather Jackson, Respondent
speaker: KAVANAUGH
text: You --

case_name: West Virginia, Et Al., Petitioners, V. B.p.j., By Her Next Friend And Mother, Heather Jackson, Respondent
speaker: GORSUCH
text: -- one more question  --oh, I'm sorry, please.

case_name: West Virginia, Et Al., Petitioners, V. B.p.j., By Her Next Friend And Mother, Heather Jackson, Respondent
speaker: Michael R. Williams
text: Please.

case_name: West Virginia, Et Al., Petitioners, V. B.p.j., By Her Next Friend And Mother, Heather Jackson, Respondent
speaker: GORSUCH
text: Go ahead. No, you're --

case_name: West Virginia, Et Al., Petitioners, V. B.p.j., By Her Next Friend And Mother, Heather Jackson, Respondent
speaker: KAVANAUGH
text: Go ahead. (Laughter.)

case_name: West Virginia, Et Al., Petitioners, V. B.p.j., By Her Next Friend And Mother, Heather Jackson, Respondent
speaker: Michael R. Williams
text: I can do both.

case_name: West Virginia, Et Al., Petitioners, V. B.p.j., By Her Next Friend And Mother, Heather Jackson, Respondent
speaker: GORSUCH
text: No, you can't do both. That's not fair. That's not fair, I mean, even -- even by our standards. You  -- you -- you make the argument that "on the basis of" means "solely because of," solely. We have long said that "because of" means but-for, not "solely because of." The rehab act speaks of "solely because of."  It seems to me an awful big stretch, counsel, to say that "on the basis of" imports anything other than but-for causation. And, you know, Comcast is against you there. And I just wonder why -- why you put your eggs in that basket.

case_name: West Virginia, Et Al., Petitioners, V. B.p.j., By Her Next Friend And Mother, Heather Jackson, Respondent
speaker: Michael R. Williams
text: So three answers, Your Honor.

case_name: West Virginia, Et Al., Petitioners, V. B.p.j., By Her Next Friend And Mother, Heather Jackson, Respondent
speaker: GORSUCH
text: And  -- and --and, by the way, isn't -- isn't -- isn't the -- the distinction here solely because of sex anyway?

case_name: West Virginia, Et Al., Petitioners, V. B.p.j., By Her Next Friend And Mother, Heather Jackson, Respondent
speaker: Michael R. Williams
text: Well, let me take each  --each of those in turn or I'll try. I don't think that the case turns on the Court accepting the idea that it's solely on the basis of sex, so I think you could stop  --

case_name: West Virginia, Et Al., Petitioners, V. B.p.j., By Her Next Friend And Mother, Heather Jackson, Respondent
speaker: GORSUCH
text: That's a sufficient answer right there.

case_name: West Virginia, Et Al., Petitioners, V. B.p.j., By Her Next Friend And Mother, Heather Jackson, Respondent
speaker: Michael R. Williams
text: Fair enough.

case_name: West Virginia, Et Al., Petitioners, V. B.p.j., By Her Next Friend And Mother, Heather Jackson, Respondent
speaker: GORSUCH
text: Thank you. Your turn.

case_name: West Virginia, Et Al., Petitioners, V. B.p.j., By Her Next Friend And Mother, Heather Jackson, Respondent
speaker: Michael R. Williams
text: Thank you.

case_name: West Virginia, Et Al., Petitioners, V. B.p.j., By Her Next Friend And Mother, Heather Jackson, Respondent
speaker: KAVANAUGH
text: Can you explain the relevance and significance of the Javits Amendment to distinguishing sports from all these other hypotheticals?

case_name: West Virginia, Et Al., Petitioners, V. B.p.j., By Her Next Friend And Mother, Heather Jackson, Respondent
speaker: Michael R. Williams
text: So I think the relevance and significance is Your Honors are faced with a unique set of regulations and that Congress was directly and intimately involved  in both the instigation of the regulation in 1974 and then sort of --

case_name: West Virginia, Et Al., Petitioners, V. B.p.j., By Her Next Friend And Mother, Heather Jackson, Respondent
speaker: KAVANAUGH
text: And in that law referred to the nature of particular sports, right?

case_name: West Virginia, Et Al., Petitioners, V. B.p.j., By Her Next Friend And Mother, Heather Jackson, Respondent
speaker: Michael R. Williams
text: It  --it did. So what they said was we want you, the agency, HEW, to  go ahead and implement Title IX writ large. And the  -- it called out one specific problem that I -- I think arose on the floor about whether Title IX applies to intercollegiate athletics, in particular, intercollegiate athletics. And I would say  --

case_name: West Virginia, Et Al., Petitioners, V. B.p.j., By Her Next Friend And Mother, Heather Jackson, Respondent
speaker: KAVANAUGH
text: And that's been extended to high school by the regulations.

case_name: West Virginia, Et Al., Petitioners, V. B.p.j., By Her Next Friend And Mother, Heather Jackson, Respondent
speaker: Michael R. Williams
text: Right, exactly.

case_name: West Virginia, Et Al., Petitioners, V. B.p.j., By Her Next Friend And Mother, Heather Jackson, Respondent
speaker: KAVANAUGH
text: But -- but ruling for you on sports does not open the door in my view given the Javits Amendment to the chess club necessarily. That could be separately analyzed, but it doesn't follow from a -- a law that says sports.

case_name: West Virginia, Et Al., Petitioners, V. B.p.j., By Her Next Friend And Mother, Heather Jackson, Respondent
speaker: Michael R. Williams
text: That's exactly right. And that's exactly why we were trying to make your job easier in the sense that we took the language expressly from the regulations and mapped it over onto our own statute. So there's really no debate, if it's outside the context of Title IX, it's outside the context of our statute. So, at that point, the Court's analysis is done. But I think, when you have a regulatory scheme where Congress was specifically involved, you know, in fact, undertook a review, then that's exactly the sort of regulation that even in a post-Loper Bright world continues to have importance because it's longstanding, continuous, contemporaneously issued, all those sorts of check boxes that this Court under a Skidmore framework continues to place substantial weight on. So I think that makes the Court's task relatively straightforward.

case_name: West Virginia, Et Al., Petitioners, V. B.p.j., By Her Next Friend And Mother, Heather Jackson, Respondent
speaker: SOTOMAYOR
text: What do you  --

case_name: West Virginia, Et Al., Petitioners, V. B.p.j., By Her Next Friend And Mother, Heather Jackson, Respondent
speaker: KAVANAUGH
text: And what about Bostock?

case_name: West Virginia, Et Al., Petitioners, V. B.p.j., By Her Next Friend And Mother, Heather Jackson, Respondent
speaker: SOTOMAYOR
text: No, no, I --

case_name: West Virginia, Et Al., Petitioners, V. B.p.j., By Her Next Friend And Mother, Heather Jackson, Respondent
speaker: KAVANAUGH
text: Do you want to deal with Bostock?

case_name: West Virginia, Et Al., Petitioners, V. B.p.j., By Her Next Friend And Mother, Heather Jackson, Respondent
speaker: Michael R. Williams
text: I -- I think -- so I guess it depends on the way in which you mean does it deal in Bostock. I think it  --

case_name: West Virginia, Et Al., Petitioners, V. B.p.j., By Her Next Friend And Mother, Heather Jackson, Respondent
speaker: KAVANAUGH
text: Well, if  --if an employer said we're going to fire all the transgender women  --

case_name: West Virginia, Et Al., Petitioners, V. B.p.j., By Her Next Friend And Mother, Heather Jackson, Respondent
speaker: Michael R. Williams
text: Right.

case_name: West Virginia, Et Al., Petitioners, V. B.p.j., By Her Next Friend And Mother, Heather Jackson, Respondent
speaker: KAVANAUGH
text: -- that would be a violation. If a school says we're not going to allow the transgender women to play sports, you say that's not a violation. Both statutes use the term "sex."  Can you explain?

case_name: West Virginia, Et Al., Petitioners, V. B.p.j., By Her Next Friend And Mother, Heather Jackson, Respondent
speaker: Michael R. Williams
text: I think the reason why is, well, to be clear, our -- our statute is very different from a specific choice to say a transgender person shall not participate because of their transgender status. And I think that really is what makes the difference between this case and Bostock, is Bostock is attacking status -based discrimination, and West Virginia would, I think, be in a much different position if we had just said transgender persons shall not compete. But that's not what West Virginia did.

case_name: West Virginia, Et Al., Petitioners, V. B.p.j., By Her Next Friend And Mother, Heather Jackson, Respondent
speaker: KAVANAUGH
text: What if it said transgender women and girls shall not compete in women's and girls' sports?

case_name: West Virginia, Et Al., Petitioners, V. B.p.j., By Her Next Friend And Mother, Heather Jackson, Respondent
speaker: Michael R. Williams
text: I think, again, that's a much closer question. I  -- I think, if we're talking about engaging with the actual status of  --

case_name: West Virginia, Et Al., Petitioners, V. B.p.j., By Her Next Friend And Mother, Heather Jackson, Respondent
speaker: KAVANAUGH
text: Do you think you could lose under Title IX with a statute that said that?

case_name: West Virginia, Et Al., Petitioners, V. B.p.j., By Her Next Friend And Mother, Heather Jackson, Respondent
speaker: Michael R. Williams
text: I think  --Bostock, I think, is -- now I understand Your Honor's question. I think Bostock raises an interesting question as to whether that reference to transgender status would in turn implicate the sex status that Title IX is meant to address. But, ultimately, I think the Court doesn't need to address that because you can stop at the first step, right?  You don't have an actual transgender exclusion that would give rise to that kind of linkage of analysis.

case_name: West Virginia, Et Al., Petitioners, V. B.p.j., By Her Next Friend And Mother, Heather Jackson, Respondent
speaker: ROBERTS
text: Thank you, counsel. In  terms of Bostock, I understand that to say that discrimination on the basis of transgender status is discrimination on the basis of sex. But the question here is whether or not a sex-based classification is necessarily a transgender classification, and I wonder if that is consistent with your understanding.

case_name: West Virginia, Et Al., Petitioners, V. B.p.j., By Her Next Friend And Mother, Heather Jackson, Respondent
speaker: Michael R. Williams
text: It's entirely consistent I would say on the equal protection side in particular and also in the Title IX context, I think, for some of the reasons I just discussed with Justice Kavanaugh. I think the Court can stop and say that a sex definition and a reference to biological sex is not the same as a transgender classification. And I think, even if we engage in -- in the sort of but-for causation analysis, I think it's as simple as saying does the result change if you change the gender identity of the individual involved?  And the reality is, if you apply the West Virginia statute to someone identifying as a -- you know, a biological boy identifying as a boy applies in the very same way as a biological boy identifying as a girl.

case_name: West Virginia, Et Al., Petitioners, V. B.p.j., By Her Next Friend And Mother, Heather Jackson, Respondent
speaker: ROBERTS
text: Justice Thomas?  Justice Alito? Justice Sotomayor?

case_name: West Virginia, Et Al., Petitioners, V. B.p.j., By Her Next Friend And Mother, Heather Jackson, Respondent
speaker: SOTOMAYOR
text: I find it strange that the district court and the court below did find a Title IX violation but not an equal  protection violation and remanded for the equal protection violation. I'm not sure how it could do that because it would seem to me that if the evidence is not sufficient to justify finding an equal protection violation, it's not sufficient to find a Title IX violation. Is that correct at least on the record as it exists now?

case_name: West Virginia, Et Al., Petitioners, V. B.p.j., By Her Next Friend And Mother, Heather Jackson, Respondent
speaker: Michael R. Williams
text: Right. And so, to be clear, the district court actually ruled for West Virginia on both Title IX and  --

case_name: West Virginia, Et Al., Petitioners, V. B.p.j., By Her Next Friend And Mother, Heather Jackson, Respondent
speaker: SOTOMAYOR
text: Right.

case_name: West Virginia, Et Al., Petitioners, V. B.p.j., By Her Next Friend And Mother, Heather Jackson, Respondent
speaker: Michael R. Williams
text: And so the Fourth Circuit said you lose on Title IX and we're not sure about equal protection.

case_name: West Virginia, Et Al., Petitioners, V. B.p.j., By Her Next Friend And Mother, Heather Jackson, Respondent

text: Mr. Chief Justice, and may it please the Court:   So there have been a lot of different arguments made this morning, and so I think it might be helpful to just focus on what I think are the easiest way to resolve both of the claims in this case. On the equal protection claim, it's the arguments we discussed this morning about intermediate scrutiny doesn't work on this as-applied basis. So let me focus for the Title IX claim. I think the simplest way to resolve the Title IX claim in this case is as follows: The regs expressly authorize sex-separated teams. The other side isn't challenging those regs. When those regs use the word "sex," they obviously use the word "sex" to mean biological sex in the reproductive biology sense. That's the ordinary meaning of the -- the term in 1972 and 1974. As a result, whether or not they are right that taking testosterone suppression eliminates any physical advantage doesn't matter because the regs define separation based on sex, based on biology, not based on circulating testosterone levels. So the difference that  --their claim that they've eliminated the difference just doesn't matter under the langu age of the regs, and that's enough to resolve the case.

And, yes, we don't think a man taking performance-altering drugs is similarly situated to a woman, but you don't even have to reach that question because, under the regs, the question is the regs say you can separate based on sex. Everyone agrees that sex in those regs means biological sex. Therefore, the circulating testosterone levels are just legally irrelevant under the regs.

case_name: West Virginia, Et Al., Petitioners, V. B.p.j., By Her Next Friend And Mother, Heather Jackson, Respondent

speaker: GORSUCH

speaker: KAVANAUGH
text: But --

case_name: West Virginia, Et Al., Petitioners, V. B.p.j., By Her Next Friend And Mother, Heather Jackson, Respondent
speaker: GORSUCH

case_name: West Virginia, Et Al., Petitioners, V. B.p.j., By Her Next Friend And Mother, Heather Jackson, Respondent
speaker: Hashim M. Mooppan
text: For two reasons. One, we think that the statute and the regs clearly do not permit the claim.

case_name: West Virginia, Et Al., Petitioners, V. B.p.j., By Her Next Friend And Mother, Heather Jackson, Respondent
speaker: GORSUCH
text: I understand that.

case_name: West Virginia, Et Al., Petitioners, V. B.p.j., By Her Next Friend And Mother, Heather Jackson, Respondent
speaker: Hashim M. Mooppan
text: And then the second is how the Spending Clause applies in the context of Title IX is, I think, a little more complicated than my friend suggested. It's not a clear statement requirement. I think, if you look at some of these clear notice cases, cases like Jackson and Geyser, I don't think you would say that those  statutes had a clear statement.

case_name: West Virginia, Et Al., Petitioners, V. B.p.j., By Her Next Friend And Mother, Heather Jackson, Respondent
speaker: GORSUCH
text: It's a clear notice requirement.

case_name: West Virginia, Et Al., Petitioners, V. B.p.j., By Her Next Friend And Mother, Heather Jackson, Respondent

case_name: West Virginia, Et Al., Petitioners, V. B.p.j., By Her Next Friend And Mother, Heather Jackson, Respondent
speaker: GORSUCH
text: Why?  I mean, your argument is that in  -- in 1974 and 1960 -- sex meant biology, and that  -- it's not clearly -- there's not clear notice otherwise. Why isn't that the end of it?

case_name: West Virginia, Et Al., Petitioners, V. B.p.j., By Her Next Friend And Mother, Heather Jackson, Respondent
speaker: Hashim M. Mooppan

case_name: West Virginia, Et Al., Petitioners, V. B.p.j., By Her Next Friend And Mother, Heather Jackson, Respondent
speaker: GORSUCH

case_name: West Virginia, Et Al., Petitioners, V. B.p.j., By Her Next Friend And Mother, Heather Jackson, Respondent

case_name: West Virginia, Et Al., Petitioners, V. B.p.j., By Her Next Friend And Mother, Heather Jackson, Respondent

case_name: West Virginia, Et Al., Petitioners, V. B.p.j., By Her Next Friend And Mother, Heather Jackson, Respondent

case_name: West Virginia, Et Al., Petitioners, V. B.p.j., By Her Next Friend And Mother, Heather Jackson, Respondent

case_name: West Virginia, Et Al., Petitioners, V. B.p.j., By Her Next Friend And Mother, Heather Jackson, Respondent

case_name: West Virginia, Et Al., Petitioners, V. B.p.j., By Her Next Friend And Mother, Heather Jackson, Respondent

text: Well, I  -- I think that's true for the funding, but I don't think that's true in terms of how the discrimination provision works. case_name: West Virginia, Et Al., Petitioners, V. B.p.j., By Her Next Friend And Mother, Heather Jackson, Respondent
speaker: GORSUCH
text: All right.

case_name: West Virginia, Et Al., Petitioners, V. B.p.j., By Her Next Friend And Mother, Heather Jackson, Respondent
speaker: GORSUCH
text: Okay. case_name: West Virginia, Et Al., Petitioners, V. B.p.j., By Her Next Friend And Mother, Heather Jackson, Respondent
speaker: Hashim M. Mooppan
text: Well, no. So, you know, Your Honor asked why we run the similarly situated argument. Take, for example  --

case_name: West Virginia, Et Al., Petitioners, V. B.p.j., By Her Next Friend And Mother, Heather Jackson, Respondent
speaker: GORSUCH
text: Don't -- don't  -- don't bring that back up. (Laughter.)

case_name: West Virginia, Et Al., Petitioners, V. B.p.j., By Her Next Friend And Mother, Heather Jackson, Respondent
speaker: GORSUCH
text: Well, okay, all right. If that's your view, then let's talk about the similarly situated. I guess I have to. case_name: West Virginia, Et Al., Petitioners, V. B.p.j., By Her Next Friend And Mother, Heather Jackson, Respondent

case_name: West Virginia, Et Al., Petitioners, V. B.p.j., By Her Next Friend And Mother, Heather Jackson, Respondent

case_name: West Virginia, Et Al., Petitioners, V. B.p.j., By Her Next Friend And Mother, Heather Jackson, Respondent

text: It's not pseudo science to say --

case_name: West Virginia, Et Al., Petitioners, V. B.p.j., By Her Next Friend And Mother, Heather Jackson, Respondent

case_name: West Virginia, Et Al., Petitioners, V. B.p.j., By Her Next Friend And Mother, Heather Jackson, Respondent

case_name: West Virginia, Et Al., Petitioners, V. B.p.j., By Her Next Friend And Mother, Heather Jackson, Respondent

case_name: West Virginia, Et Al., Petitioners, V. B.p.j., By Her Next Friend And Mother, Heather Jackson, Respondent

case_name: West Virginia, Et Al., Petitioners, V. B.p.j., By Her Next Friend And Mother, Heather Jackson, Respondent

case_name: West Virginia, Et Al., Petitioners, V. B.p.j., By Her Next Friend And Mother, Heather Jackson, Respondent

case_name: West Virginia, Et Al., Petitioners, V. B.p.j., By Her Next Friend And Mother, Heather Jackson, Respondent

case_name: West Virginia, Et Al., Petitioners, V. B.p.j., By Her Next Friend And Mother, Heather Jackson, Respondent

case_name: West Virginia, Et Al., Petitioners, V. B.p.j., By Her Next Friend And Mother, Heather Jackson, Respondent

case_name: West Virginia, Et Al., Petitioners, V. B.p.j., By Her Next Friend And Mother, Heather Jackson, Respondent

case_name: West Virginia, Et Al., Petitioners, V. B.p.j., By Her Next Friend And Mother, Heather Jackson, Respondent

case_name: West Virginia, Et Al., Petitioners, V. B.p.j., By Her Next Friend And Mother, Heather Jackson, Respondent

case_name: West Virginia, Et Al., Petitioners, V. B.p.j., By Her Next Friend And Mother, Heather Jackson, Respondent

case_name: West Virginia, Et Al., Petitioners, V. B.p.j., By Her Next Friend And Mother, Heather Jackson, Respondent

text: Well  --

case_name: West Virginia, Et Al., Petitioners, V. B.p.j., By Her Next Friend And Mother, Heather Jackson, Respondent
speaker: BARRETT
text: Mr. --

case_name: West Virginia, Et Al., Petitioners, V. B.p.j., By Her Next Friend And Mother, Heather Jackson, Respondent

case_name: West Virginia, Et Al., Petitioners, V. B.p.j., By Her Next Friend And Mother, Heather Jackson, Respondent

case_name: West Virginia, Et Al., Petitioners, V. B.p.j., By Her Next Friend And Mother, Heather Jackson, Respondent

case_name: West Virginia, Et Al., Petitioners, V. B.p.j., By Her Next Friend And Mother, Heather Jackson, Respondent

case_name: West Virginia, Et Al., Petitioners, V. B.p.j., By Her Next Friend And Mother, Heather Jackson, Respondent

case_name: West Virginia, Et Al., Petitioners, V. B.p.j., By Her Next Friend And Mother, Heather Jackson, Respondent

case_name: West Virginia, Et Al., Petitioners, V. B.p.j., By Her Next Friend And Mother, Heather Jackson, Respondent

case_name: West Virginia, Et Al., Petitioners, V. B.p.j., By Her Next Friend And Mother, Heather Jackson, Respondent

case_name: West Virginia, Et Al., Petitioners, V. B.p.j., By Her Next Friend And Mother, Heather Jackson, Respondent
